title: The Blaschka Object Network — Harvard Digital Archive Corpus Register
repository: Archives of the Economic Botany Herbarium of Oakes Ames / Botany Libraries, Harvard University
collection: The Archives of Rudolf and Leopold Blaschka and the Ware Collection of Blaschka Glass Models of Plants, 1886–2020

current_catalogue_snapshot.metric_guard: HOLLIS 'digital content' is a catalogue/component metric, not a count of letters or digitised pages. Do not describe the collection as containing 897 digitised letters.

scope: Harvard's large digital and physical archive for the Ware Collection, treated as a corpus architecture rather than one source. The register separates correspondence, artwork, labels, photographs and fragile physical ephemera, and records which layers HOLLIS states are already digitised.

subseries.title: Blaschka correspondence from studio
subseries.scope_note: Chiefly Rudolf Blaschka correspondence to his parents Leopold and Karolina during his 1892 United States trip and summer 1895, plus miscellaneous family and Glass Flowers documents.

subseries.title: Ware correspondence
subseries.scope_note: Correspondence kept by Mary Lee Ware and Elizabeth Ware, arranged chronologically. No correspondence is listed for 1917–1919. The bulk is among Rudolf Blaschka, George Lincoln Goodale, Mary Lee Ware and Oakes Ames.

digital_layers.research_value: Visual source corpus for reference drawing, observation, model planning and workshop representation.

digital_layers.series: Series V. Ware Collection of Glass Flower Models — Model and section labels
digital_layers.research_value: Object-document crosswalk: scientific naming, sectioning, mounting and later collection identification.

digital_layers.series: Series V. Ware Collection of Glass Flower Models — photographic images
digital_layers.research_value: Display, teaching, conservation and visual afterlife of the models.

physical_layers.series: Series III. Blaschka ephemera and artifacts
physical_layers.research_value: Material evidence for packing, mailing, workshop tools and glass handling that cannot be reduced to correspondence.

direct_digital_examples.description: Rudolf Blaschka letter to George Lincoln Goodale, 6 January 1896

related_source_systems.name: BHL Rudolf Blaschka letters to Walter Deane, 1895–1927
related_source_systems.relationship: separate digitised correspondence corpus held by Harvard Botany Libraries and published through BHL; overlaps chronologically and socially with ecb00006 but must retain its own provenance and metadata

related_source_systems.name: Rakow Research Library, Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka Archive
related_source_systems.relationship: workshop-side archive with drawings, notebooks, business records and correspondence; Harvard HOLLIS points researchers to digitised Rakow material as related sources

ingest_strategy.phase_1: Download the HOLLIS finding-aid CSV and create a component-level inventory preserving call number, hierarchy, date, box/folder and digital-link fields.
ingest_strategy.phase_2: Harvest digital-surrogate URLs for Series I correspondence and map individual digital objects to the finding-aid hierarchy.
ingest_strategy.phase_3: Cross-walk dates and correspondents with BHL Deane and the local Rakow OCR corpus while retaining repository provenance as a first-class field.
ingest_strategy.guard: Do not deduplicate texts across Harvard, BHL and Rakow solely because dates or correspondents match. Copies, drafts and enclosures can be distinct documentary witnesses.

source_quality_note: This archive changes the corpus-building problem: a large part of the Harvard correspondence universe is already digitally accessible. The bottleneck is normalization and cross-walking rather than repository discovery.
